defect_origin: fork commit f1b7aebff8c2 (Federico Ficarelli 2022-08-25, [LLVM/PULP/SNITCH] Support for PULP and Snitch cores/platforms) added PULPFixupHwLoops.cpp incl. splitMBBAt and the LoopEnd block; same 4 verifier errors on xpulp-hwloop.ll with toolchains/ref-18 and port-19 llc
root_cause: Four independent verifier violations in the PULP Hardware Loop Fixup output: (1) blocks the pass creates had no/wrong live-ins: fixupLoopInstrs' LoopEnd block got none; splitMBBAt stepped back only to after lp.setup (count register missing) and used addLiveOuts (added pristine CSRs) -> 'Using an undefined physical register'; (2) the LoopEnd block has the header as CFG successor (hardware back edge) but no terminator says so -> 'MBB has unexpected successors' (on the LoopEnd block, not the lp.setup block as F005 guessed; the lp.setup block is already unanalyzable because LOOPsetup is a non-branch terminator, which the verifier accepts); (3) the pass's nops were built with x0 as a use in operand 0 -> 'Explicit definition marked as use'; (4) nops padding a <4-byte loop were inserted after the LOOPsetup terminator in the same block -> 'Non-terminator instruction after the first terminator' (138 of 495 fuzz builds, seeds 1-165).
fix: (1) computeAndAddLiveIns for each created block (LoopEnd, split setup block, pad block), as RISCVExpandAtomicPseudoInsts.cpp:421 does; (2) new zero-size terminator PseudoLOOPend <header> at the end of the LoopEnd block (Hexagon ENDLOOP0 design, HexagonPseudo.td:92 / HexagonMCInstLower.cpp:98), analyzeBranch treats it as unanalyzable (as ARM does for t2LoopEnd, ARMBaseInstrInfo.cpp:417), asm printer emits nothing; (3) nops define x0; (4) padding nops go into a new block between the setup block and its fall-through block (not at the start of that block: other blocks may jump to its label; a first attempt that did so changed the jump target in fuzz seeds 938/960 -O3 and was discarded). LOOP0/1setup definitions unchanged (making them branches would change earlier passes' code).
code_change: None in object code or debug information (.text, .debug_line and the rest of the DWARF identical with -g, DW_AT_producer aside). Assembly text: when a loop is nop-padded, one extra local label line precedes the nops and later .LBB numbers can shift.

review_response: Review REJECT (tasks/20/F013.review.json): the marker produced a .debug_line row with -g. Fixed with isMeta = 1 (as requested) AND an empty DebugLoc on the marker: with isMeta alone, 26 of 200 fuzz objects (seeds 7001-7200 -g -O2, e.g. 7008) still differed, rows losing is_stmt, because DwarfDebug::findForceIsStmtInstrs (DwarfDebug.cpp:2334-2463 at llvmorg-20.1.8) takes the last located instruction of a block (meta or not) as its outgoing line; the marker carried the lp.setup's line. With both changes all -g objects are identical.
